instruction: networkx's node_connectivity and minimum_node_cut (networkx/algorithms/connectivity) give wrong answers on directed graphs, and self-loops and parallel edges throw them off on any graph. The node connectivity of a digraph is the smallest local node connectivity over all ordered pairs of nodes (s, t), and a minimum node cut is a smallest set of nodes whose removal leaves the digraph not strongly connected; a weakly but not strongly connected digraph has node connectivity 0 and an empty minimum node cut. Today both can report values that are too large, and minimum_node_cut can return a set that does not disconnect anything, or an empty set for a strongly connected digraph. For example DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0), (3, 0)]) must give node connectivity 0 and minimum_node_cut set(), and the directed triangle DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)]) node connectivity 1 and a one-node minimum cut whose removal leaves it not strongly connected. minimum_st_node_cut(G, s, t) returns the empty set only when there is an edge from s to t: in a digraph an edge from t to s does not stop s from being separated from t (on the directed triangle, minimum_st_node_cut(G, 0, 2) == {1} and minimum_st_node_cut(G, 0, 1) == set()). Self-loops and parallel edges do not change node connectivity or node cuts: a complete graph on 5 nodes keeps node connectivity 4 and a 4-node minimum cut with a self-loop on every node, and as a MultiGraph with every edge doubled, undirected and as to_directed(). Every result must hold with each flow_func the functions accept. Results that are right today, including every undirected simple graph's, must not change. Add tests.
notes: networkx tuning task (October 4, 2026; user decision to add networkx as a tuning repository to find tasks where Sonnet 5.5 medium fails). Python 3.12 with no numpy/scipy: tests that need them are skipped, and none of the hidden tests do. networkx is not pip-installed in the benchmark venv, so its conftest warns about a "Mixed NetworkX configuration" (the nx_loopback test backend); results are the same on base and reference.
